discovery: Ultrapure hexagonal boron nitride crystals and their use as the substrate and encapsulant that enabled high-quality van der Waals heterostructures

nominees.name: Kenji Watanabe
nominees.affiliation: National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS), Tsukuba, Japan

nominees.name: Takashi Taniguchi
nominees.affiliation: National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS), Tsukuba, Japan

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional materials and van der Waals heterostructures
motivation: Watanabe and Taniguchi grew hexagonal boron nitride single crystals of exceptional purity using high-pressure, high-temperature methods. In 2010 Dean and colleagues showed that hBN is an atomically flat, inert dielectric, and that graphene placed on it reaches mobilities and homogeneity far beyond anything possible on SiO2. Assembling layers on hBN, and later encapsulating them in it, became the universal platform of 2D-materials physics. This platform made possible the fractional quantum Hall effect in graphene, Hofstadter's butterfly in moiré superlattices, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle graphene, 2D magnetism, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states and much more. NIMS crystals appear in thousands of papers from hundreds of groups around the world. This is a rare case of materials craftsmanship and a conceptual step in device design together opening an entire field of emergent quantum phenomena.
